messages.content: I need to be in downtown Minneapolis for an operations review on Thursday, May 14. It starts at 9:30 a.m. and should finish at 4:00. Compare flying from Chicago that morning against going Wednesday evening.
I’ll compare nonstop round trips from both O’Hare and Midway, including realistic time to deplane and reach downtown. Are you traveling alone, and is the review near the central business district?
Just me. The office is near Nicollet Mall and 8th Street.

For a 9:30 arrival at that office, I would plan to reach MSP no later than about 7:45 a.m. The light rail takes roughly 30 minutes to Nicollet Mall, while a car commonly takes 20 to 30 minutes but can run longer during the morning commute. Allowing time to get off the aircraft and walk through the terminal, an arrival after 8:00 leaves little recovery room.

The viable same-day flights are concentrated around 6:00 a.m. departures. I’m checking the return against a realistic departure from the office after 4:00 rather than treating 4:00 as an airport arrival time.
Right. I probably won’t be outside before 4:15. I won’t check a bag.

The strongest same-day plan is a nonstop from ORD departing at 6:05 a.m. and arriving at MSP at 7:36 a.m. At that hour, you could reasonably be at the office between 8:30 and 8:55 by car, with the light rail producing a similar or slightly later result. That gives you at least 35 minutes before the review.

For the return, a 6:45 p.m. nonstop from MSP reaches ORD at 8:17 p.m. Leaving the office at 4:15 should put you at the terminal around 5:00 to 5:20, giving you workable security margin without a checked bag. The current round-trip economy fare is $412.
Is there anything from Midway that gets me there with the same cushion?

The earliest useful Midway nonstop departs at 6:20 a.m. and arrives at 7:52 a.m. A normal transfer would put you near Nicollet Mall around 8:45 to 9:05. It can work, but it has less protection against a delayed departure or heavy traffic. Its return leaves MSP at 6:25 p.m., which is also tighter after a 4:15 office departure. The round trip is $376.

The $36 savings does not compensate for the reduced margin on both ends of the day. ORD is the more workable same-day option.
Agreed. Now show me the best Wednesday evening version. I don’t need to arrive especially early, but not after 10:00 p.m.

The best evening-before plan departs ORD Wednesday at 7:10 p.m. and arrives at MSP at 8:42 p.m. That is late enough to preserve most of the workday but should still get you to a downtown hotel around 9:30. Paired with the same Thursday 6:45 p.m. return, the airfare is currently $438.

There is a 5:35 p.m. outbound for $419, arriving at 7:07, but it requires leaving for O’Hare during the afternoon. The 7:10 departure is the cleaner schedule for only $19 more.
How do the two plans compare once timing risk is included?

Same day is cheaper before lodging: $412, no hotel night, and an expected office arrival around 8:30 to 8:55. Its weakness is that a delay of roughly 45 minutes could consume most of the buffer, and a longer disruption could make you late.

Wednesday evening costs $438 plus one hotel night and local transportation, but it removes the meeting-arrival risk. You could leave a downtown hotel shortly after 9:00 and walk to the office. The return is equally workable in both plans: leave the office around 4:15 for the 6:45 flight.

For schedule reliability, Wednesday evening is clearly stronger. For cost and avoiding an extra night, the 6:05 a.m. ORD departure is still defensible.
Any meaningfully later return, in case the review runs over?

There is an 8:05 p.m. nonstop from MSP arriving at ORD at 9:38 p.m. It adds $27 to either itinerary. That gives you room for the review to run until about 5:15 without creating airport stress. A later 9:20 departure exists, but it reaches Chicago close to 11:00 and does not improve the fare.
Keep the 6:45 return for now. Carry the 6:05 same-day option and the 7:10 Wednesday option into the hotel and total-cost comparison. Don’t book either one.

I’ll carry forward these two alternatives for the May 14 Minneapolis review:

Same day: ORD-MSP Thursday, 6:05-7:36 a.m.; MSP-ORD Thursday, 6:45-8:17 p.m.; $412 round trip.

Evening before: ORD-MSP Wednesday, 7:10-8:42 p.m.; the same Thursday return, 6:45-8:17 p.m.; $438 round trip before lodging.

Nothing has been booked. The next comparison will add a Wednesday-night downtown hotel and ground transportation so the full cost difference is explicit.
